title: Momentus Performance k6
description:
In-flight health view of a k6 load run streamed via the agentless OTLP intake, laid out to mirror the NeoLoad run overview: summary blocks for transactions, requests, throughput and VU iterations, then load-generator CPU/RAM, then errors overlaid on user load, then the three NeoLoad 'Values' tables (transactions, requests, errors) as per-row detail.

Every aggregation below was validated against a run's published k6-metrics.json.gz rather than taken on trust: first build 20260811.3 (838 requests / 969 transactions / 66 iterations), then two dedicated runs that closed out the percentile columns and the error tables. The rules that came out of that are below, and the widgets depend on all of them:

1. Counts and totals pin their bucket with .rollup(sum, 60). Do not switch to .as_rate(), which divides by an inferred interval that moves with the zoom level, and do not drop the rollup from a count, which lets Datadog collapse export points instead of summing their sample counts (838 samples read back as 784). Which scalar tiles carry it is decided by one thing: an ungrouped count that can reach for .as_count() drops the rollup, while a count taken off a distribution has no .as_count() to reach for and must keep it. The seven tiles that drop it are Failed checks, Failed, Dropped, Passed, Error rate %, Throughput Total and VU iterations Completed. .as_count() already forces sum-based time aggregation there, so both forms returned the same total on every aligned window measured, Failed reading 24 both ways and Dropped 32 both ways, while adding the rollup drops any window holding no minute boundary and default_zero then paints the gap as a green zero (379 read as 0 over 30s, 457 as 0 over 90s, 457 as 261 over a misaligned 3 minutes). Measured again on the 40s window 15:17:10-15:17:50 of the 2026-08-18 15:10 run: 2 failed checks without the rollup against 0 with it, and 106 responses without it against blank with it. Failed and Dropped carried the rollup until that check and read a green 0 over a 40s window holding 10 real request failures, which is the false negative this rule exists to prevent. Passed, Error rate %, Throughput Total and VU iterations Completed carried it until the 2026-08-19 sweep, and blanked over the 40s window 08:56:10-08:56:50 of the 17-Aug run where the three export points in range total 5,728 and .as_count() alone returns 5,728. None of those four wraps default_zero, so they blanked rather than reading a false zero, which made them cosmetic where Failed and Dropped were a false negative. Three tiles keep the rollup and always will, because they read count: or sum: off the group_duration and http_req_duration distributions where .as_count() does not exist and dropping it triggers the 838-into-784 collapse above: Transactions Total and both Avg. duration tiles, whose denominators keep it too since the distribution-sum numerator blanks the ratio regardless. Those three still blank on a window holding no minute boundary. That is the floor of the metric type rather than an oversight, so do not sweep their rollups off for consistency. The per-minute timeseries widgets do keep the rollup, because a chart plots the buckets themselves instead of reducing them to a single number, so a bucket the window excludes is simply a bar not drawn rather than a total understated.

2. Averages are a sum/count formula, never the avg: prefix. With a scalar aggregator the avg: prefix takes an unweighted mean of per-interval means, so an interval holding one sample counts as much as one holding twenty: it read a true 429.01ms mean request duration as 1139.89ms and a true 355.93ms mean transaction as 397.66ms.

3. Percentiles merge their sketches with an explicit .rollup(300) and reduce with max, so each figure is the worst 5-minute merge window rather than the whole run. Without that rollup the percentile is averaged across 10s export intervals and reads far too low (a true 5372ms p95 on saveeventcopy read as 2436ms). Two measured constraints set the interval. A bucket is keyed by its start timestamp at fixed multiples of the rollup from epoch, and the widget only sees buckets whose timestamp falls inside the window, so a view landing wholly between two boundaries goes blank however much data it holds: at .rollup(900) the window 08:55-09:00 returned nothing on all 47 transactions while 09:00-09:03 returned every one. This is alignment, not width, so widening the window is not reliably the cure and a rollup shorter than the window can still blank. And the bucket must stay wide enough to resolve the tail, because at 2-3 samples per minute a per-bucket percentile cannot see its own outlier and reducing with max does not recover it: .rollup(60) read a 3222ms p95 on copyserviceorders_04_searchevent as 1232ms while a 4731ms sample sat in the window. 300 satisfies both, and it is the interval to keep, but it is not free. Measured against 900 on build 20260817.1 it returned an identical value on every cell, 47 transactions and 45 requests across p50/p90/p95/p99, while rendering on the 5-minute views where 900 came back blank. That equivalence does not generalise. On build local-3, an 8-minute run that fell inside one 900s bucket but split across two 300s ones, 6 of 83 rows diverged and five of the six read lower at 300: saveeventcopy returned 6780.8ms against 12413.2ms at 900, a 45% under-read, with the true 95th-percentile sample sitting at 15894.9ms. That is the straddling effect one interval down, so a whole-run percentile on this board under-reads the tail whenever the window splits into more than one bucket. The trade is deliberate: a blank widget on the 5-minute views was the worse failure. Do not lower it to 60, and do not read this column as the whole-run tail: rule 7 covers the exact table that carries that.

4. Metrics are prefixed k6perf., not k6. Datadog's k6 integration owns the k6.http_req_* namespace and stamps its own metadata over those names, under which the histogram's count and max sub-values stop resolving and both reads fall back to the interval sum. Names the integration does not claim (group_duration, iteration_duration, think_time) were always exact. The Min/Max/percentile columns on the requests table are the ones this unblocks, and they are now confirmed: on a dedicated run read back against its own artifact, Min/Max/Avg/Count are exact to 0.00% across all 25 rows of both detail tables.

5. A percentile column is a sketch estimate, not a computed percentile, so judge it by whether each value traces to a real observation. Every one of 81 table cells and 116 timeseries points sat within 0.79% of an actual sample, and each column landed near its nominal rank (p90 at the 88th-94th, p95 at the 92nd-98th, p99 at the 96th-98th percentile of the run). No rank formula reproduces the values, and recomputing them the way k6 does, by interpolating on (n-1), manufactures apparent errors up to 89% that are purely definitional. The real limit is resolution: at the 6-9 samples per row a 300s bucket holds under this profile the sketch cannot separate adjacent percentiles, and on 14 of 25 rows two adjacent columns returned an identical value. Narrowing the bucket from 900 to 300 did not change this, since every cell returned the same value at both. Read p99 per row as 'somewhere in the tail', not as a figure distinct from p95.

6. default_zero() never appears in a grouped query or a grouped table formula. On a window with no run it manufactures a zero-valued series where none existed, and because that series carries no group tags the table renders a phantom row reading N/A / N/A / N/A with one 0 in it. The plain ratio needs no help: measured on the validation run, failed_count / response_count returns 0 on every row that has data and returns nothing at all on an empty window, which is exactly the wanted behaviour in both cases. The ungrouped count tiles (Failed checks, Failed, Dropped) do keep default_zero, because a single-value tile has no rows to invent and would otherwise read blank on a clean run, leaving 'no failures' and 'query broken' looking identical.

7. A percentile that has to be exact does not come from the live feed at all. group-aggregator.cjs computes count, avg, min, med, p90, p95, p99 and max per transaction over every sample in the run, using k6 own interpolation method, and summary-forwarder.cjs posts them once when the run ends as k6perf.transaction.* gauges tagged scenario and transaction. Read with max: and no rollup they are exact and window-independent, which is what the exact whole-run tail table shows: on build local-3, copyevent_06_clicksave read 13225.91ms there against 8041.7ms from the 300s sketch and 12413.2ms from 900s, and crystalreport_02_login 21899.58ms against 21691.29ms from both. Verified end to end against that run own group-series.csv, all 48 rows and all eight statistics matching to the decimal. The cost is that the points land when the run ends, so the table is empty while a run is in flight and does not respond to zooming into a sub-window: the sketch table above it is the one to watch live. All eight statistics carry a column, Min and Med included. An exact median is the one figure on the row that exposes skew against Avg, which the sketch p50 never could: on build local-3 the SignIn request under book_event reads Med 561.17ms against Avg 1702.25ms and p99 17503.42ms. The same feed runs one level down for requests, request-series.csv posted as k6perf.request.* tagged scenario, transaction and request, so the requests table carries the exact tail its sketch percentiles cannot resolve either. It adds roughly 1,300 gauge timeseries against a run existing 7,952 and an org allotment of 36,375, so its marginal cost is zero (docs/datadog-cost-model.md). The forwarder is gated by the same DD_API_KEY flag as the other two feeds and skips silently without it, leaving group-metrics.csv unchanged either way.

The 'Where request time goes' chart stacks http_req_sending, http_req_waiting and http_req_receiving, which sum exactly to http_req_duration (22.567696761336798ms of bands against 22.56769676133679ms of duration on build 20260817.1), and carries blocked + connecting + tls_handshaking as a separate line because connection setup sits outside duration. Its bands are averages rather than percentiles because percentile aggregation is enabled only on http_req_duration and group_duration, so a pNN query against any component metric returns nothing, and enabling it is forward-only with no backfill.

The k6perf.agent.* series come from the CI resource sampler via metric-forwarder.cjs, not from k6, so they carry no scenario tag and the $scenario variable does not filter them.

The '/active min' tiles and the '/active min' table columns average the pinned 60s bucket across only the minutes carrying traffic, so under per-iteration pacing they read above the whole-run average: the validation run showed 121 transactions/min against a whole-run 89. The data metrics span one fewer active bucket than the request metrics, so the Throughput tile's divisor is not identical to the Requests tile's. Both Throughput tiles divide by 1e6 and label the result MB, because data_received and data_sent are byte counters that carry no unit metadata in Datadog and rendered as a bare 791.6 M. The scaling is decimal to match k6's own summary, so a run that stays under a megabyte reads 0.0.

This is a sanity check during a run, not the reporting surface: the published k6 artifacts (report.html, group-metrics.csv, k6-metrics.json.gz) remain authoritative. See docs/datadog-live-metrics.md.

All transactions: one row per k6 group, sorted by average duration. Percentiles are the worst 5-minute merge window, not the whole run.

definition.content:
Metrics carry aggregated counts, not per-event rows, so these tables answer 'which request or check is failing, with what status' rather than NeoLoad's timestamped error list. For individual occurrences read the console log and report.html in the published k6-results artifact. A network-level failure (timeout, reset) arrives as status 0 with a k6 error_code; an HTTP failure carries the real status.

All three of these are value-verified against an artifact. Failed checks matched exactly on two runs (7 on copy_event / T004_CopyEvent_04_SearchEvent / Source event found; later 1 + 1 on the two savecrystalreport checks). Dropped iterations matched a run that hit k6's default 10m maxDuration: 32 dropped, and 16 per active minute across the two minutes carrying them. Failed requests matched exactly on a run built to emit deliberate failures against a local endpoint: three rows (500/1500, 404/1404, and a refused connection as 0/1212) with Errors 10/6/4, Errors per minute 5/3/2 across two active minutes, and Avg and Max equal to the artifact to four decimals. A refused connection reports 0 ms, so a zero in those two columns is real data, not a broken query.
